repo_prior_art.cite: none; the closest catalogue entries concern pointwise/private CATE or discrete ATE heterogeneity, not this continuous Hölder homogeneity-testing experiment

published_prior_art.cite: CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 gives an asymptotic sieve test for constant CATE under much stronger smoothness, not this fixed-sample minimax equality region
KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 supplies a pointwise-CATE fuzzy-hypothesis construction, not a constant-CATE-null fixed-sample testing converse on the same class
DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026 and Yu2026VarianceHTE give asymptotic homogeneity tests; neither supplies the stated three-index fixed-sample matched minimax radius

novelty_flags.label: related_work / Open-ended Question 2
novelty_flags.one_line: CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 is a substantially closer direct predecessor—an asymptotic nonparametric test of the constant-CATE null—but is listed only in the bibliography and never compared against the proposed fixed-sample Hölder modulus.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:null-supported-converse
soundness_flags.one_line: The symbol c is declared as the null constant in I=[-1/2,1/2] but is also used as the positive separation multiplier in H1(c r_sharp); introduce distinct c_null∈I and c_sep>0.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The publication studies minimax Hölder-smooth CATE estimation and gives a localized-fuzzy-hypothesis lower bound plus a local-polynomial estimator under additional conditions; it is not a constant-CATE testing theorem.
The paper derives critical-radius upper and lower bounds for conditional-independence testing with continuous conditioning variables under smooth conditional-law restrictions.

source_verification_receipts.version: JASA accepted author version posted online 18 May 2026; theorem text corroborated against arXiv:2410.00985v4
source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher record; arXiv v4 Sections 4, D, and E, including Theorems 2, 4, and 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work proposes quantitative and qualitative CATE-homogeneity tests with asymptotic distribution, fixed-alternative, and local-alternative analyses over structured rule classes, rather than a fixed-sample minimax Hölder radius.

The paper targets the variance-zero CATE null using intra-fold splitting and proves asymptotic normality and type-I control under nuisance learner conditions; it gives no shrinking fixed-sample minimax class.

source_verification_receipts.version: working-paper text corresponding to the published Review of Economics and Statistics article; published theorem text not directly accessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The direct predecessor formulates a nonparametric test of whether the CATE is constant and gives asymptotic null validity and consistency for sieve alternatives under strong smoothness assumptions.
The paper considers L2-separated smooth goodness-of-fit alternatives, records the nonadaptive minimax detection boundary, and establishes the iterated-logarithmic adaptation cost.
PCM concerns conditional-mean-independence testing via projected covariance and spline-based asymptotic theory, not an observational CATE homogeneity minimax frontier.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair oeq:null-supported-converse by separating the null constant c_null from a strictly positive lower-bound multiplier c_sep, and propagate the renamed symbols through its handle and lower-bound target.

Add a dedicated CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 row to related_work, explaining its constant-CATE null, sieve asymptotics, smoothness restrictions, and why it neither gives finite-sample uniform calibration nor the three-index minimax radius.

Before Stage 0, make the no-penalty theorem a sharper boundary result by deriving at least one complementary strict-penalty sequence from an explicit sub-frontier; this makes the experiment-comparison contribution informative even if the complete map remains difficult.

recommended_next_step: Revise the symbol collision and add the omitted direct Crump et al. comparator, then continue this angle to Stage 0; the core otherwise retains a potentially flagship matched-minimax kernel.
